heading: India news Highlights, 21 September 2026: Naga teenager shot dead by suspected militants in Manipur’s Tamenglong
paragraphs: A 17-year-old Naga youth was shot dead by suspected militants in Manipur’s Tamenglong district on Monday, police said. NK Wiphenbou was walking alone from Upper Nkou village to Tamei town when he was attacked around 10.30 am. Naga village volunteers later found his body along a narrow path.

Former Manipur chief minister N Biren Singh condemned the killing and called for those responsible to be brought to justice. Naga People’s Front legislator Awangbou Newmai also condemned the incident, describing it as an attack on civilians. Officials said more than 40 people have been killed since clashes broke out between Naga and Kuki communities in February.

If you are just joining us, this is The Indian Express Realtime breaking news blog – where we bring you the latest news updates of the day in real time. Scan the top headlines of the day here, or keep scrolling to see the latest updates stream in.

The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert for six Kerala districts — Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam and Thrissur — valid from 7 am on Monday, with heavy to very heavy rainfall and thunderstorms with surface winds of up to 40 kmph likely at isolated places. Chief Minister VD Satheesan has directed the state’s rain situation to be assessed hourly, and SMS alerts have been issued in Idukki and Kottayam districts. Collectors in both districts have been directed to assess conditions and initiate evacuation if needed. On Sunday, four people were killed in separate landslip incidents in Idukki and Kottayam, while heavy rain triggered a flash flood on the Kottapuzha River in Nilambur, Malappuram, sweeping away six people. (PTI)

An Indian Express investigation has found that the Indian branch of ICBC, China’s largest state-owned bank, was placed on a watchlist by financial regulators in the aftermath of the 2017 Doklam standoff — a surveillance step triggered by the geopolitical crisis 2,000 km away. Despite being on the watchlist, the bank subsequently cleared a $500 million loan to Vedanta, a transaction that regulators later flagged — raising questions about how geopolitical risk assessments translate into financial oversight at foreign-owned institutions operating in India.

Sulphur import prices have more than trebled over the past year as attacks on energy infrastructure in Russia and West Asia disrupt global supply chains — a supply shock with direct consequences for India’s fertiliser sector and food prices, since sulphur is a critical input for superphosphate and other agricultural inputs.

Tata Trusts have challenged N Chandrasekaran’s use of a casting vote to reappoint himself as chairman of Tata Sons — a governance dispute that has brought the boardroom feud between the Tata group’s founding trusts and its professional leadership into open confrontation, with significant implications for the group’s long-term succession structure.

Nila Vikhe Patil, niece of Maharashtra minister Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil, has been elected to the Swedish Parliament — a first for the family and a rare instance of the Indian diaspora’s second generation making an entry into European national legislatures.

An undertrial inmate was allegedly stabbed to death by two fellow prisoners inside Central Jail No. 10 in Delhi’s Rohini on Monday, police said. The deceased, identified as Pradeep alias Mohinder, 31, was lodged in judicial custody in a murder case. He was allegedly attacked with a sharp-edged weapon while returning to his barrack and sustained a stab injury to his neck. He was taken to BSA Hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.

Pradeep’s family alleged that jail staff failed to provide timely assistance after the attack. His sister Nisha claimed he was taken to hospital nearly an hour later and questioned how a sharp-edged weapon entered the jail premises. Police said a case was being registered at Samaypur Badli police station, while CCTV footage was being examined and the circumstances surrounding the stabbing were being investigated.

A 17-year-old Naga youth was shot dead by suspected militants in Manipur’s Tamenglong district on Monday, police said. NK Wiphenbou was walking alone from Upper Nkou village to Tamei town when he was attacked around 10.30 am. Naga village volunteers later found his body along a narrow path.

Former Manipur chief minister N Biren Singh condemned the killing and called for those responsible to be brought to justice. Naga People’s Front legislator Awangbou Newmai also condemned the incident, describing it as an attack on civilians. Officials said more than 40 people have been killed since clashes broke out between Naga and Kuki communities in February.

A Delhi court has granted bail to a 22-year-old Zomato delivery boy accused of entering a house using a duplicate key and stealing gold and silver jewellery and Rs 30,000 in cash. Additional Sessions Judge Hargurvarinder Singh Jaggi said the accused’s young age and the possibility of being incarcerated with hardened criminals as a first-time offender had to be considered.

The court noted that the stolen articles had been recovered and the investigation completed, marking a significant change since his earlier bail plea was rejected in July. The accused was granted regular bail on a personal bond of Rs 15,000 with one surety of the same amount, with conditions including joining the investigation when called and not contacting witnesses or tampering with evidence.

The Supreme Court on Monday dismissed a plea seeking directions to prevent people from attempting suicide by jumping into animal enclosures at zoos. A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta passed the order while hearing a challenge to a July 2020 Delhi High Court order.

The high court had declined to entertain the plea alleging inaction by the Centre and concerned authorities over repeated such incidents but allowed the petitioner to approach the authorities with a representation. The Supreme Court observed that requisite safeguards were already in place and said, “Everyone is supposed to act as per the law.” The plea had cited incidents of people jumping into tiger and lion enclosures, some of which resulted in deaths.

Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan on Monday said the state government would implement the Centre’s new Labour Codes without adversely affecting workers’ rights. Addressing a leadership meeting of the Congress-affiliated Indian National Trade Union Congress (INTUC), Satheesan said the codes could not be left unimplemented as they were laws passed by Parliament.

Satheesan said the government would take into consideration suggestions made by INTUC while implementing the codes and ensure that the process did not harm the state’s labour sector. He also said that if the codes were not implemented, workers could be left without legal protection. The Centre had announced the implementation of the four Labour Codes in November last year, consolidating 29 existing labour laws.

Kerala Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob on Monday said authorities would examine whether soil excavation carried out as part of National Highway works contributed to landslide concerns along the road to Munnar and nearby areas in Idukki. His remarks came after visiting a woman injured in a mudslide at Vattavada, where two people died after a shed was flattened by the mudslide on Sunday.

Jacob said the district was under an orange alert and urged people to temporarily avoid travelling to Idukki amid continuing rain. He said officials would seriously examine the circumstances surrounding the soil excavation and investigate any irregularity. He also said ongoing National Highway construction was causing traffic blocks and that he had asked the project director to ensure machinery was positioned to allow vehicles to pass.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday reviewed preparations for the ‘Vettri Payanam’ free bus travel scheme for women, which is set to be launched on October 2. The scheme will expand free travel beyond ordinary city and hill buses to include Express, LSS and Deluxe buses in metropolitan and urban areas, as well as Mofussil Ordinary and Ghat Ordinary buses covering longer distances in hill areas.

Under the expanded scheme, 12,692 of the 18,413 scheduled buses operated by seven state transport corporations will be covered, accounting for 69 per cent of the fleet. Around 84.32 lakh women are expected to benefit daily, while electronic ticketing machine linking has been completed. Testing is scheduled by September 25, followed by a trial run on September 27.

The Social Democratic Party of India (SDPI) has demanded that the Karnataka government grant official language status to Urdu, following the state Cabinet’s decision to accord Tulu the status of a second additional administrative language in Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts. SDPI Karnataka general secretary Afsar Kodlipete welcomed the recognition for Tulu but questioned the government’s approach towards Urdu and Urdu-medium education.

Kodlipete cited the 2011 Census and claimed that Urdu speakers account for a larger share of Karnataka’s recorded mother-tongue population than Tulu speakers. He also raised concerns over vacancies in Urdu-medium schools and said the approval of 800 Urdu-medium teacher posts was insufficient. The SDPI said it was not opposed to the development of Tulu but sought equal recognition and protection of the linguistic and educational rights of Urdu speakers.

Purnima Sah from Bombay reports that Prof Doolla has been removed from the post of Dean (Administrative Affairs), while clarification states that he has not been suspended. He previously served as Dean (Student Affairs).

Brendan Dabhi from Ahmedabad reports that Gujarat Police declared bomb threats against the Somnath temple and the BJP office in Ahmedabad to be hoaxes after conducting comprehensive security sweeps, including evacuations and inspections by specialized units like the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad. The initial intelligence inputs were reportedly relayed from the Punjab Police, though neither the temple authorities nor the BJP office received any direct communication regarding the threats. Following these investigations, it has been determined that this specific story will not be published on the web.

ACP Advait Gandhi said, "Around 9 am, we received an input from the State Intelligence Bureau, Gandhinagar, according to which there was a bomb threat targeting the BJP Central Office in Khanpur. Following the alert, the Bomb Detection and Disposal Squad (BDS) conducted a thorough check. Necessary local arrangements have been made, and the situation is currently normal... A threat was also received concerning the Somnath Temple and the BJP office in Koba... As for who sent the email and its origin, that is a matter under investigation... Nothing suspicious has been found so far."
The India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement will come into force from October 20, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said.

"The New Zealand-India Free Trade Agreement has been ratified today and will enter into force on 20 October 2026, unlocking new access for New Zealand businesses to one of the fastest-growing markets in the world," New Zealand's Ministry of Foreign Affairs & Trade said.

DMK chief MK Stalin has opposed the proposed new Secretariat at Foreshore Estate near Chennai’s Marina Beach, citing concerns over fishermen’s livelihoods and the neighbourhood.
"We will 'crush' TVK regime's arrogance which has not withdrawn order on new Secretariat despite opposition from parties backing it," he said.

Mumbai activist and postgraduate student Harshada Borade alleged that Anti-Terrorism Cell personnel searched her western suburbs residence without a warrant from Friday evening until early Saturday, after she attended a kite-flying programme supporting Palestinian children, according to news agency PTI.
The Mumbai police allegedly searched the residence after she took part in the event.
The officials confirmed that an inquiry was underway, and a background check was being conducted and that no FIR has been registered so far.
In a video posted on social media, Borade claimed that after the police searched her house, her landlord asked her to look for a new residence, stating she could no longer stay there.
Six children drown while bathing in pond in Bihar’s Bhagalpur district, say police.
IIT Bombay has clarified that its Director has not resigned, categorically stating that reports claiming otherwise are false.

IIT Bombay issued an apology over earlier communication concerning Sahil’s death, saying details leading up to the incident remain under investigation.

"We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil. The details and circumstances leading up to the incident remain subject to investigation by the appropriate authorities. In view of the ongoing investigation, it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process," the institution said in a post on X.

Amaal Sheikh from Delhi reports that the Supreme Court has ruled that police cannot mechanically re-arrest an accused individual released due to violations of Article 22, which mandates informing an arrestee of the grounds of arrest and producing them before a magistrate within 24 hours. A bench led by Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul Chandurkar characterised these as fundamental principles governing personal liberty rather than mere procedural requirements, asserting that any breach renders an arrest unconstitutional regardless of the nature or gravity of the offence. Under the new procedure, if an agency seeks re-arrest, it must provide written grounds and apply to a jurisdictional magistrate explaining the necessity of custody and the circumstances of the previous violation, with the application endorsed by the investigating officer's superior. Furthermore, the superior must transfer the investigation to another officer and initiate a departmental inquiry into the initial lapse. This judgment stems from the case of Shiromani Akali Dal leader Jaskaran Jeet Singh Deol, who was previously released after police failed to furnish written grounds for his arrest.
As Vande Mataram ended abruptly after two stanzas in the Karnataka Assembly, BJP MLAs recited its full version in the House.
The Supreme Court has agreed to constitute a special bench to hear the NHAI’s plea challenging directions to build shelters for stray cattle across the country, according to news agency PTI.

Himanshu Harsh from Patna reports that a teenage boy and girl returning from coaching classes in Jamui, Bihar, were surrounded, assaulted, and molested by a group of men on September 19, an incident captured in videos that circulated on social media. In the footage, the victims are seen pleading with their attackers, who were also filmed chasing them and physically mistreating them. Following the emergence of these videos, the Jamui police have initiated an investigation, identified the suspects, and are actively working to track them down for arrest, despite the absence of a formal complaint.

Raakhi Jagga from Patiala reports that Jagseer Singh, a resident of Namol village in Sangrur, Punjab, attempted suicide by consuming poison outside the Deputy Commissioner’s office on Sunday after allegedly facing harassment and assault for speaking out against the local drug trade. Singh, who had previously posted a video regarding the availability of "chitta" in his village, claimed he was assaulted by the village sarpanch, Sukhwinder Singh "Sukhi" Punia, and that his family was intimidated, while asserting that authorities failed to act on his complaints. Currently recovering in a Patiala hospital, Singh's case has sparked significant political backlash, with opposition leaders including Bikram Singh Majithia, Ravneet Singh Bittu, and Partap Singh Bajwa targeting the AAP government for its failure to curb the drug menace in Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's home district and protect those who speak against it.
The Supreme Court has agreed to urgently list Mamata Banerjee’s plea challenging the Election Commission’s decision to freeze her party’s name and symbol.
Indian Naval Ships Sahyadri and Kulish arrived at Subic Bay in the Philippines on September 20 to participate in the ADMM-Plus Joint Cooperation Activity.

The participation of Indian Naval Ships in the ADMM-Plus JCA is in consonance with the Government of India’s Act East Policy and the vision of MAHASAGAR, underscoring India’s continued commitment to multilateral maritime cooperation and constructive engagement with regional partners. The deployment will provide opportunities for the Indian Navy to interact with participating maritime forces through professional and operational engagements, contributing to greater understanding of shared maritime challenges.

Pragynesh from Delhi reports that a 56-year-old tailor has been arrested following the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl in a popular Central Delhi market on September 16. According to police, the accused lured the victim into his shop while she was purchasing stationery, where he restrained and assaulted her before the girl reported the incident to her parents. An FIR has been registered under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, and the suspect is currently in judicial custody. This incident follows a separate recent case in Outer North Delhi, where a teenage girl was allegedly gang-raped and killed by four individuals, all of whom have been apprehended by the police.
Police detained J&K Apni Party leaders protesting over various issues against the J&K government outside the Civil Secretariat in Srinagar amid the Autumn Session of the legislative Assembly.

A woman from Agra who climbed a tower in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area, near the CM's residence, alleged that Mann Singh had encroached on her 1.5 bighas of land and threatened her.
"My name is Tulsa. I am from Agra. Mann Singh has encroached upon my 1.5 bighas of land. He threatens me," she told news agency ANI.

#watch | A woman from Agra, who had climbed a tower on Hazratganj's Park Road near the CM's residence, allegedly over a land dispute, was evacuated by the Lucknow Fire Department and Police. Further details awaited. pic.twitter.com/jsd7rTPTNf

Bengaluru cyber police have arrested three men—Amit Mishra, Tausif Ahmed, and Parashuram Sadanand Kannanavar—in connection with a large-scale online trading and investment scam that defrauded a city resident of nearly Rs 94 lakh. The investigation uncovered a sprawling network involving over 500 mule bank accounts operated from hotels, where the accused utilized fraudulent "ZNPAY" and SMS-forwarding apps to intercept banking credentials and funnel proceeds into Binance crypto wallets. Digital forensics have linked the operation to IP addresses in Kolkata, Hong Kong, and California, prompting authorities to coordinate with the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre (I4C) as they investigate the potential international scope of the fraud and a broader web of associates.
A 56-year-old man was arrested after a class 6 student was allegedly sexually assaulted inside a shop in Delhi’s Sadar Bazar area, police said, according to news agency ANI.

A case under relevant sections of rape laws, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and wrongful confinement was registered at the Women Police Station based on the victim's complaint.

"A class 6 student was allegedly sexually assaulted after her hands and legs were tied inside a shop in Delhi Sadar Bazar area. The girl had gone out to purchase stationery items when the incident allegedly took place. A case under relevant sections pertaining to rape, the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and wrongful confinement was registered at the Women Police Station on the basis of the victim's complaint. The 56-year-old accused, identified as Maksud, was arrested on Friday in connection with the case. Further investigation is underway," the Delhi police said.
The Chokkad flash flood in Kerala has claimed six lives after the Kottappuzha River overflowed following heavy rain, with five bodies recovered so far.

Heavy rains continue to batter the Idukki district in Kerala, triggering a major landslide at Pazhampallichal in Adimali that destroyed one house and blocked vehicular traffic, following a previous incident in Munnar-Vattavada.

A major tragedy was averted after five families narrowly escaped by relocating just in time before the debris and floodwaters struck. While residents and Fire and Rescue Services personnel work to clear the roads, authorities have successfully evacuated families from the hazardous zone to a newly established relief camp at the LP School in Palisakkallu.

The IIT Bombay student suicide case has been transferred to the Mumbai Police Crime Branch, which will investigate the allegations against Professor Suryanarayan Dulla.
The father of the deceased has accused the professor of making casteist remarks to the deceased student, said the Mumbai police, according to news agency ANI.
Sensex jumped 448.32 points to 74,743.28 in early trade, while the Nifty gained 50.3 points to 23,396.70 as Indian benchmark indices opened higher.
